blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Understanding contact and tactile magnitude in hand-object interaction is a key step toward physically intelligent systems, yet learning such representations is limited by the cost and restricted coverage of tactile measurements. We present Touch-JEPA, a framework for learning tactile representations from hand-object videos with limited tactile supervision. We first introduce a self-supervised pretraining objective that learns from video alone without tactile supervision. Using video-derived hand geometry, Touch-JEPA predicts masked visual features at corresponding hand-surface locations from spatial and temporal context, encouraging the representation to capture latent contact dynamics. We then extend this formulation to joint representation learning, where masked prediction is applied to all videos while tactile supervision is available only for a labeled subset, grounding the shared representation in measured contact and magnitude. With self-supervised pretraining alone, simple supervised readouts on frozen Touch-JEPA features outperform supervised baselines in contact discrimination and tactile magnitude estimation across three human-hand benchmarks, and transfer to robotic hands without robot tactile training data. Joint learning with limited tactile supervision further improves contact and magnitude estimation on the human-hand benchmarks. Together, these results show that hand-object video can provide scalable self-supervision for tactile representation learning, while limited tactile measurements provide complementary physical grounding.
blocks.zh: 了解手物体相互作用中的接触量和触觉量是朝着物理智能系统迈出的关键一步,然而,学习这种表达因触觉测量的成本和覆盖范围有限而受到限制。 我们介绍Touch-JEPA,这是在有限的触觉监督下从手物体视频中学习触觉表现的框架。 我们首先引入了一个自我监督的预训目标,这个目标单独从视频中学习而无需触觉监督. Touch-JEPA利用视频衍生的手几何技术,从空间和时间角度预测相应手表位置的蒙面视觉特征,鼓励表现以捕捉潜在的接触动态. 然后,我们把这一提法扩大到联合代表学习,即对所有视频采用蒙蔽的预测,而触觉监督只用于标有标签的子集,从而将共享的表示建立在测量接触和规模的基础上。 单靠自我监督的预训,在冷冻的Touch-JEPA上简单的有监督的读取功能在接触歧视和触觉大小估计上就超过了监督的基线,在三种人手基准上,在没有机器人触觉训练数据的情况下转移到机器人手中。 在有限的触觉监督下进行联合学习,进一步改善了接触和对人手基准的规模估计。 这些结果一起表明,手物视频可以为触觉表现学习提供可伸缩的自超视觉,而有限的触觉测量则提供互补的物理地面.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Physical understanding of hand-object interaction underpins contact-rich manipulation ( Xue et al., 2025 ) , the transfer of dexterous skill from human video to robots ( Qin et al., 2022 ; Shaw et al., 2023 ) , and clinical hand-function assessment ( Zhao and Zariffa, 2024 ) . Yet visual observations reveal hand-object geometry and motion while contact state and tactile magnitude remain only indirectly observable ( Grady et al., 2022 ) . Learning representations that capture such tactile information from visual and temporal cues could therefore provide a richer understanding of hand-object interaction beyond geometry and motion ( Zhao et al., 2025 ) .

blocks.en: Prior work has largely approached tactile understanding from video through supervised prediction. Early approaches exploited load-related visual cues, including soft-tissue deformation, fingertip color changes, and cast shadows, to predict planar pressure maps ( Grady et al., 2022 ; Grady et al., 2024 ) . More recent methods extend this setting to pressure on 3D hand meshes ( Zhao et al., 2025 ; Jeon et al., 2026 ) , forces on hand and object meshes given object geometry ( Ilic et al., 2026 ) , and dense hand-surface contact across diverse interactions ( Jung and Lee, 2025 ) . Alongside these methods, paired hand-object video and sensor datasets have enabled supervised learning and evaluation for pressure prediction, contact estimation, retrieval, and classification ( Song et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2026b ; Zhou et al., 2026b ; Zeng et al., 2026 ) . These advances show the potential of learning tactile information from visual observations, but depend on paired tactile measurements for supervision.
blocks.zh: 先前的工作主要是通过有监督的预测,从视频中了解触觉。 早期方法利用了与负载有关的视觉提示,包括软质问题变形、指尖颜色变化和投影,以预测平面压力图(Grady等,2022;Grady等,2024)。 较新的方法将这种设置扩大到对3D手型甲壳虫的压力(赵等,2025;Jeon等,2026;手型力和物体甲壳虫给物体几何(Ilic等,2026;)),以及不同相互作用之间密集的手相接触(郑和李,2025)。 除了这些方法之外,配对的手物体相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机相机 这些进步显示了从视觉观测中学习触觉信息的潜力,但依靠配对的触觉测量来进行监督.

blocks.en: However, paired tactile data are difficult to acquire at scale ( Jiang et al., 2024 ) . Collecting such supervision often requires specialized hardware and careful calibration. Moreover, tactile gloves alter bare-hand appearance ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) , planar sensors restrict contact geometry, and instrumented objects limit object diversity ( Brahmbhatt et al., 2019 ) . Simulation and derived contact labels alleviate some of these sensing constraints but often depend on task-specific pipelines ( Wang et al., 2022 ) . Consequently, existing tactile datasets provide strong physical grounding but only fragmented coverage of hand regions, objects, and interactions.
blocks.zh: 然而,配对触觉数据在规模上难以获得(Jiang等,2024.). 收集这种监督往往需要专门的硬件和仔细的校准。 此外,触觉手套会改变光手外观(张等,2026b),平面传感器会限制接触几何,有仪器的物体会限制物体的多样性(Brahmbhatt等,2019). 模拟和衍生出的联系标签减轻了部分这些感知限制,但往往取决于特定任务管道(Wang等,2022.). 因此,现有的触觉数据集提供了很强的物理地基,但只是零散地覆盖了手区域、物体和相互作用。

blocks.en: In contrast, large-scale video datasets capture diverse hand-object interactions across broad visual and behavioral distributions, but lack explicit tactile annotation ( Damen et al., 2022 ; Grauman et al., 2022 ) . Our key insight is that tactile supervision and large-scale unlabeled video provide complementary learning signals: tactile measurements ground the representation in physically meaningful quantities, while diverse interaction videos provide broader spatial, anatomical, and temporal context. Self-supervised masked prediction ( Assran et al., 2025 ) can therefore leverage unlabeled videos to learn interaction regularities beyond the limited tactile-labeled subset, while explicit tactile supervision preserves grounding in contact and magnitude. Together, these signals enable tactile representations to benefit from both physically grounded supervision and the scale and diversity of natural interaction videos.
blocks.zh: 相形之下,大型视频数据集则捕捉到跨广视和行为分布的不同手物相互作用,但缺乏明显的触觉注释(Damen等,2022;Grauman等,2022.). 我们的主要见解是,触觉监控和大规模无标签的视频提供了互补的学习信号:触觉测量以物理上有意义的数量定位了表现,而不同的互动视频则提供了更广泛的空间、解剖和时间背景。 因此,自我监督的被蒙蔽的预测(Assran等,2025年)可以利用无标签的视频,在有限的触觉标记子集之外学习相互作用的规律性,而明确的触觉监督则保留了接触和规模上的基础. 这些信号加在一起,使触觉表现能够从物理上的监督以及自然互动视频的规模和多样性中受益.

blocks.en:
We introduce Touch-JEPA, a framework for tactile representation learning from hand-object interaction videos with limited tactile supervision. In the self-supervised setting, Touch-JEPA learns from
video without tactile annotations through masked prediction.
Video-derived hand geometry defines corresponding
hand-surface locations, allowing visual features to be
predicted from spatial and temporal interaction context
across heterogeneous videos. A Geometry Encoder integrates evidence across hand regions and frames under interaction and anatomical masking. We then extend the framework to joint representation learning, where the JEPA objective is applied across all videos while tactile supervision is available only for the labeled subset. The two objectives share the encoder, allowing tactile measurements to ground the learned representation in contact and magnitude while self-supervised prediction continues to exploit the scale and diversity of the broader video distribution. We further control interference between the two learning signals during joint training to preserve their complementary information. Our contributions are summarized below:

blocks.en: • We introduce Touch-JEPA, a unified tactile representation learning framework that treats abundant hand-object video and limited tactile measurements as complementary sources of supervision: video provides scalable interaction coverage, while tactile measurements provide direct physical grounding of the shared representation. • We propose a geometry-guided self-supervised pretraining objective that learns tactile-relevant hand-surface representations from video alone. Touch-JEPA predicts masked latent features at anatomically corresponding surface locations, using video-derived hand geometry together with interaction and anatomical masking to integrate spatial and temporal evidence without requiring tactile annotations. • We develop a joint representation learning strategy that incorporates tactile supervision from a limited labeled subset while retaining self-supervised learning across all videos. Tactile supervision shapes the shared encoder and its EMA teacher, allowing physically grounded information to propagate through representation-level self-distillation without tactile pseudo-labels, while gradient control preserves the complementary learning signals.

Tactile Representation and Estimation. Instrumented gloves enable dense hand-object contact sensing ( Sundaram et al., 2019 ; Song et al., 2025 ) , while prior work learns tactile
representations through autoencoding, cross-modal self-supervision, and
cross-sensor alignment ( Murali et al., 2018 ; Zambelli et al., 2021 ; Yang et al., 2022 ; Kerr et al., 2022 ; Yang et al., 2024 ; Feng et al., 2025 ; Wi et al., 2026 ) .
Recent methods further use masked visuo-tactile reconstruction or joint-embedding
objectives for tactile observations ( Zhu et al., 2025 ; Higuera et al., 2024 ) .
Tactile-JEPA ( Kovtun et al., 2026 ) applies joint-embedding prediction to the
signals of distributed tactile sensors, whereas
Touch-JEPA learns touch from video and never takes a tactile signal as input.
A complementary line of work estimates tactile quantities from vision, including
dense contact ( Jung and Lee, 2025 ) , planar pressure ( Grady et al., 2022 ; Grady et al., 2024 ) , hand-surface pressure ( Zhao et al., 2025 ; Jeon et al., 2026 ) , and joint hand-object forces ( Ilic et al., 2026 ) .
Paired video-tactile datasets support supervised prediction ( Zhou et al., 2026b ; Zeng et al., 2026 ) , and concurrent work scales such
supervision with large glove recordings and RGB-only inference ( Zhang et al., 2026a ; Zhou et al., 2026a ) .
These methods, including vertex-token video models ( Jeon et al., 2026 ) , are trained on
tactile or contact labels.
In contrast, Touch-JEPA learns tactile representations from video without tactile
targets during self-supervised pretraining and evaluates whether contact and tactile magnitude
can be decoded from the resulting frozen features.

self-distillation and masked prediction ( Caron et al., 2021 ; Zhou et al., 2021 ; Oquab et al., 2023 ; Siméoni et al., 2025 ) .
Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn by predicting unobserved
representations in images ( Assran et al., 2023 ) and videos ( Bardes et al., 2024 ; Assran et al., 2025 ; Mur-Labadia et al., 2026 ) , and such video encoders
already capture fine-grained physical-contact cues ( Alrasheed et al., 2026 ) .
Related work combines representation prediction with geometric, generative,
or action objectives.

Given a hand-object interaction video, the y y -encoder processes unmasked RGB to produce target visual features at geometry-aligned hand-surface locations. The x x -encoder combines masked RGB with estimated hand
geometry to predict these targets. When tactile annotations are available, joint training additionally supervises contact and magnitude predictions decoded from masked x x -encoder states before the predictor, providing complementary physical grounding for the shared representation.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We presented Touch-JEPA, a unified framework that combines self-supervised learning of tactile-relevant representations from hand-object video with tactile supervision on a labeled subset. Geometry-guided masked visual prediction enables contact and sensor-native magnitude estimation through supervised readouts on frozen features. Joint training further improves human-hand estimation, with particular benefits under limited tactile supervision. The self-supervised representations also transfer to robotic hands and support simulated manipulation, demonstrating their utility beyond tactile estimation.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了Touch-JEPA,这是一个统一的框架,将自学手取物视频的触觉相关表现与被标注子集的触觉监督相结合。 几何制导的蒙面视觉预测能够通过对被冻结特征的监督读取来进行接触和感应-内分量估计。 联合培训进一步改善了人工估计,在有限的触觉监督下特别有利。 自我监督的表示方式也转移到了机器人手上,并支持模拟操纵,表明其效用超出了触觉估计.

blocks.en: Limitations and Future Work. Magnitude results are sensor-specific and do not establish cross-sensor force calibration. Within-contact temporal correlations remain low on some datasets, where limited tactile variation within 16-frame clips constrains the evaluation of fine-grained temporal tracking. Future work includes pretraining on more diverse and longer videos, improving robustness to geometry errors, and evaluating manipulation across broader tasks and on physical robots. Additionally, the joint-embedding framework could be extended to incorporate language or sensor inputs during representation learning.

blocks.en:
Hand geometry provides correspondence between image observations and a common anatomical surface.
Vertex and joint coordinates are centered at the wrist and divided by the root mean squared vertex distance to the wrist in each frame.
Vertex attributes additionally include surface normals, mesh visibility, and image inclusion.
The anatomical positional encoding sums a vertex embedding, a region embedding, six-frequency Fourier features of the template coordinates, and a linear embedding of normalized frame index.
Joints use joint identity and frame index.
An additional palm frame, defined by the wrist, index metacarpophalangeal joint, and ring metacarpophalangeal joint, supplies canonical coordinates through zero-initialized affine projections.
The same zero-initialized side input also carries the frame’s rotation and the wrist position divided by hand size, so the global hand pose remains available ( 18 18 inputs per vertex and 15 15 per joint).
The original camera-oriented coordinates remain available.
Geometry estimation is frozen throughout training.

Physics runs at 120 120 Hz with two substeps. A calibrated RGB camera
records 384 × 384 384\times 384 images at 4 4 Hz with a 55 55 -degree field of view.
Each encoder input contains the trailing 16 16 actual frames, spanning 3.75 3.75 seconds and ending at the current observation. Although the
backbone is noncausal within this window, it receives no frames after
the decision time. The input is the full camera image with ImageNet
normalization.

blocks.en:
Planning minimizes the scene and surface distance in
Equation 10 with a one-step horizon.
Reference observations at demonstration endpoints 2 2 , 4 4 , 14 14 , and 18 18 provide successive subgoals
for 2 2 , 2 2 , 10 10 , and 4 4 decisions.
Each encoder computes its own reference features
using its training normalization.
Predicted robot state is rolled forward by the predictor
but does not enter the goal distance.

blocks.en:
At each planning decision, the cross-entropy method
samples 400 400 candidates for 10 10 refinement iterations
and retains 10 10 elites.
The search variables are three palm translations and
one grip value, which is copied to the five hand commands.
Initial search standard deviation is 0.7 0.7 ,
with a floor of 0.03 0.03 .
Translation is limited to an L1 norm of 7.5 7.5 cm
per decision and a fixed workspace.
The controller executes the projected final mean through
inverse kinematics and a smooth joint ramp.

blocks.en: H.4 Baselines and Evaluation Criteria
blocks.zh: H.4 基线和评价标准

blocks.en:
The V-JEPA 2.1 baseline uses the same released visual backbone
initialization, camera observations, fitted geometry, trajectories,
predictor training budget, subgoal schedule, CEM settings, and controller
as Touch-JEPA-AC. Its surface input samples concatenated features from
backbone blocks 5 5 , 8 8 , and 11 11 , followed by a fixed orthonormal
projection to 768 768 channels and the same vertex grouping.
Thus, its surface tokens have width 768 768 , compared with Touch-JEPA’s
learned width 256 256 . Predictor input and output projections accommodate
this difference.
